about.newsletterDescription: Get a weekly digest of the best events. No spam, just the good stuff.
about.subscribeError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
about.openingParagraph1: We were the students who kept missing out.
about.openingParagraph2: Tony found an Instagram story about Italian cooking lessons for $5. It was posted 3 days ago. The event was already over.
about.openingParagraph3: Erica heard about Man Dancing: Hip-Hop Edition from a poster in the hallway. 30 minutes before it started. She showed up, and it was packed.
about.openingParagraph4: The next week, she found out about a Mechanical Arm curling competition in a random Discord. That's when we realized: all the coolest events are hidden.
about.photo1Caption: One of the dozens of events we found out about too late.
about.phase2Paragraph1: We were sitting in the SLC, complaining about missing yet another event (this time it was free Chipotle at a Women in Engineering mixer), when Erica said: "Why isn't there just... one place for all of this?"
about.phase2Paragraph3: Tony handled the backend—scraping club Instagrams, linking up with WUSA feeds, building the filter logic. Erica designed everything: the illustrations, the hand-drawn icons, the color palette.
about.phase2Paragraph4: The first version was rough. But it worked.
about.photo2Caption: Late nights in the SLC. Tony on backend, Erica on design.
about.phase3Paragraph1: We posted the link in a few group chats. Then we made a poster (ironic, we know) and stuck it in the SLC. Within a week, people were texting us screenshots.
about.phase3Paragraph2: "Wait, there's a Repair Club? I can actually fix my bike there?"
about.phase3Paragraph3: Someone found the Gatka Club (Sikh martial arts) through Wat2Do and said it was the highlight of their term. Another person discovered Retro Rollers (roller skating meetups) and made six new friends in one night.
about.phase3Paragraph4: That's when we realized: this isn't just a calendar. It's a way to discover the version of campus life you didn't know existed.
about.photo3Caption: People started discovering events they never knew existed.
about.todayParagraph1: Wat2Do is used by hundreds of students to discover events they'd otherwise miss. From Bloomberg networking panels to Motor Boat cruises to Video Game tournaments.
about.todayParagraph2: We don't run ads. We don't sell your data. We just think campus life should be easier to navigate.
about.todayParagraph3: If you find this useful, tell a friend.
about.guideDescription: Here's what we've learned about making the most of campus events.
about.guideIndustryWie: WiE × Bloomberg Panel: Real engineers who actually answer questions honestly. Plus, they usually bring snacks.
about.guideIndustryAtlassian: Atlassian Coffee Chats: Way less intimidating than a career fair booth. You can actually have a conversation.
about.guideIndustryStartup: Startup Career Fair: Skip the big corporate booths. Go straight to startups where you can talk to actual founders.
about.guideRandomRepair: Repair Club: Broke your laptop charger? These folks have tools and will teach you how to fix it yourself. Completely free.
about.guideRandomGatka: Gatka Club: Sikh martial arts with wooden sticks. No experience needed. Underrated.
about.guideRandomRetro: Retro Rollers: Roller skating at local rinks. Great for de-stressing during midterms.
about.guideFriendsFood: Free Food Events: Sort by "Food Provided" in the filters. Pro tip: show up 15 minutes early.
about.guideFriendsGames: Game Nights: Perfect low-key hangout. Most clubs provide the games.
about.guideFriendsWonderland: Canada's Wonderland Trips: Various clubs organize discounted group trips. Way cheaper than going solo.
about.footerPS: P.S. We don't run ads. Everything runs out of our own pockets. No data selling. Just students helping students.
